interactions.note: You get one Reaction per round. An Opportunity Attack taken before the trigger leaves nothing for the readied response, and a readied response that has fired leaves nothing for a later Opportunity Attack. Tested both ways.
Ready is the turn's action. You can't ready after attacking, and you can't attack after readying.
Trigger timing during movement: the Reaction comes right after the triggering step, mid-move (ambiguity 3). A goblin that steps in and out of reach also offers an Opportunity Attack.
Holding the spell is Concentration. Readying ends an earlier Concentration such as Bless (ambiguity 1), and damage calls for a Constitution save that can make the spell dissipate (#9).
The slot is spent when you ready. It isn't refunded if the trigger never comes or Concentration breaks, and the release spends no second slot.
A readied slot spell is cast on your turn, so it counts toward that turn's one slot spell. Releasing it on another creature's turn shouldn't count again. Not tested yet.
A held Magic Missile released at a target that has Shield available would offer Shield. Not tested: no SRD monster in scope casts Shield.
The tests name targets in the readied response and never check range at release. Reading A or B can come later without changing these tests.

interactions.with: Healing Word, Shield, Fire Bolt (casting times)
interactions.note: Bonus Action and Reaction spells are refused. An action cantrip can be readied.

Readied movement is capped at Speed. It's unclear whether a Speed-0 condition gained between readying and the trigger stops the move, and whether readied movement uses up next turn's movement (gap). Not tested.
Out of scope: the fixtures are level 1 and Extra Attack is level 5.
'Perceivable' for an invisible creature: hearing it may still count. Not tested; the register has no ruling.

abuse.case: Taking two Reactions in one round (Opportunity Attack, then readied attack)
abuse.reason: There is one Reaction per round, so the readied response has nothing left.

abuse.case: Taking two Reactions in one round (readied attack, then Opportunity Attack)
abuse.reason: After the readied attack, leaving reach must not provoke a second Reaction.

abuse.case: Acting out of turn (readying on another creature's turn)
abuse.reason: You take the Ready action on your turn.

abuse.case: Taking two actions in one turn (attack, then Ready)
Chained commands: readying an action plus a move as one response
abuse.reason: The response is either the action or a move up to Speed, not both.

abuse.case: Moving farther than Speed allows through a readied move
abuse.reason: Readied movement is up to your Speed.

abuse.case: Naming a creature that doesn't exist in the trigger
abuse.reason: A trigger about a creature that isn't there can't be perceived.

abuse.case: Spending spell slots that don't exist (readying a spell with no slot)
abuse.reason: The readied spell is cast as normal and expends its slot.

abuse.case: Getting the slot back when the readied spell is never released
abuse.reason: Resources are expended when the spell is readied.

abuse.case: Keeping Concentration on two spells (Bless plus a held spell)
abuse.reason: Holding the spell requires Concentration (ruling proposed).

abuse.case: Readying a Bonus Action or Reaction spell
abuse.reason: A readied spell must have a casting time of an action.

abuse.case: A refused command that still costs the turn or a slot
abuse.reason: assert_refused_cleanly checks that the state is unchanged, and the slot count is asserted.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready ambiguity 1: 'holding on to the spell’s magic requires Concentration'. Does holding a spell that isn't itself a Concentration spell end an existing Concentration?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A. Holding any readied spell is an effect that requires Concentration, so readying it ends Concentration on an earlier spell (for example Bless), as GLOSS.concentration says.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready ambiguity 2: 'take your Reaction right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger'. Does an ignored trigger use up the readied action?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A. Ignoring the trigger keeps the readied action, and the Reaction, for a later occurrence of the same circumstance before the start of your next turn.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready ambiguity 3: 'right after the trigger finishes'. For a movement trigger, does the Reaction resolve after the triggering step or after the whole move?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A. The Reaction resolves right after the triggering step and interrupts the rest of the move. The mover then carries on with its remaining movement.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready gap: what happens to a held spell that is never released before the start of your next turn?
rulings_proposed.ruling: The Concentration that holds it ends at the start of your next turn, the spell dissipates without effect, and the spent slot isn't refunded.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready #4: is the readied response checked when you ready it or only when the trigger occurs?
rulings_proposed.ruling: It is checked when you ready it. A response that isn't one action (a Bonus Action, or an action plus movement) or one move up to your Speed is refused cleanly on your turn, before the action is spent.

output.summary:
The engine has no Ready action. It has no `ready` command, no structured trigger and no readied Reaction, and stage B found no code. I wrote 29 tests, all claimed red and marked xfail(strict) with one shared ticket. They cover every clause, #1 to #9, with positive and negative tests, boundary tests for #2, #4 and #8, and 12 abuse tests.

I ran them with --runxfail, and every one fails only on "Unknown command 'ready'", never in its own setup. The normal run gives 134 passed, 33 xfailed for tests/srd. ruff format and ruff check are clean.

The tests use a command shape I proposed: `{"cmd": "ready", "actor", "trigger": {"event": "moves_within", "creature", "feet"}, "response": <command dict without actor>}`. When the trigger occurs, the engine asks the readier `game.decide(actor, "readied", [True, False])`: True takes the Reaction, False ignores the trigger. The shape lives only in the new tests/support/ready.py, so if the dev loop picks a different one, only that helper changes. Every test goes through Session.execute.

The tests also cover how Ready combines with other rules:
- **Reactions:** one per round, so an Opportunity Attack before the trigger uses up the readied response, and a fired readied response leaves no Opportunity Attack.
- **Concentration:** a held spell needs Concentration, readying ends an earlier Bless, a failed save makes the held spell dissipate and a successful one keeps it.
- **Slots and casting time:** the slot is spent when you ready and isn't refunded; Bonus Action and Reaction spells are refused, action cantrips are allowed.
- **Speed:** a readied move is capped at your Speed.

Five rulings are proposed: Concentration reading A, an ignored trigger can be answered later, the Reaction interrupts the rest of a move, an unreleased held spell dissipates with the slot lost, and the response is checked when you ready it. Ambiguity 4 (choosing targets at release) is not tested yet. I added the new cheats to loop/abuse-catalogue.md. No scenario changes, since stage B had no verdicts.
